what_it_is: the observed distribution of (quantized - original) accuracy in percentage points on OpenLLM-style benchmarks, per quantization scheme, with a split-conformal 90% interval. It is a calibrated historical baseline, NOT a per-model predictor.

training_data.source: RedHatAI model cards on Hugging Face

prospective_strict.note: excludes rows whose family is in training, and Llama-4 (parser was adapted to that card family)

known_limitations: No interval excludes zero, so the tool can never say a config WILL cost accuracy -- only that damage is probably bounded.
19 of 25 observed losses worse than 3pp fall BELOW the interval floor. Large degradations are exactly where it fails.
Trained only on checkpoints Red Hat chose to publish, so it underpredicts damage from an untuned recipe (outcome-truncated training data).
Reads exactly 2 inputs: quantization scheme, and size band via 6 size-dependent widths. It reads no family, benchmark or base accuracy.
Cells refused for insufficient measured calibration: w4a16|<2B, w8a16|>10B. For these the tool emits no interval.
MoE and reasoning-distilled models are not separately validated.
